+
+def test_beyond_last_page_returns_empty():

+
+def test_empty_input_returns_empty():
+    assert paginate([], 1, 2) == []
+
+
+def test_invalid_page_returns_empty():

contract_tests: paginate(range(1, 8), 2, 2) == [3, 4] (literal issue example, one-based page 2, size 2) — tests/test_pagination_regression.py::test_page_two_size_two_returns_third_and_fourth
paginate(range(1, 8), 2, 2) returns a range object (slice of range input preserves input type) — tests/test_pagination_regression.py::test_page_two_size_two_returns_third_and_fourth
paginate(range(1, 8), 5, 2) == [] and paginate(range(1, 8), 100, 2) == [] (beyond last page returns []) — tests/test_pagination_regression.py::test_beyond_last_page_returns_empty
paginate([1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7], 2, 2) == [3, 4] and returns a list (list input yields list slice) — tests/test_pagination_regression.py::test_returns_list_slice_for_list_input

edits.new:
start = (page - 1) * page_size
    return items[start : start + page_size]
edits.old:
start = page * page_size
    return items[start : start + page_size]

patches.rationale: The bug: `start = page * page_size` treats page numbers as zero-based, so page 2 size 2 on range(1,8) returns items[4:6] == [5,6] instead of [3,4]. Fix by converting the one-based page to a zero-based start index: `start = (page - 1) * page_size`. The guard `page < 1 or page_size < 1` already preserves empty/invalid inputs (returns []), and slicing beyond the last page naturally returns []. Add a new regression test file covering the literal example, boundary behavior, and preservation of existing semantics.
